The result is that there are linear contractions $A$, $B_0$ with $P_sF_s=2^{2\alpha^2}B_0P_tF_tA$.
Put $N=C\mathsf T\mathsf D$. In $(Nu)_j$ the summand with index $j$ is exactly $u_j$: the factor in $\mathsf D$ cancels the Gaussian weight at the selected coordinate.
Since $\alpha^2<p$ and $\theta>p/\alpha^4$, $\alpha^2\theta>p/\alpha^2>1$, so $\|N-I\|<1/2$ and $N$ is invertible by the Neumann series $N^{-1}=\sum_i(-1)^i(N-I)^i$.
Set $\mathsf S'=\mathsf S/2$, $\mathsf J'=N^{-1}/2$, $\mathsf D'=2^{-(2\alpha^2-2)}\mathsf D$, which are contractions with norms below $3/4$, $7/8$, $1$

As $C\mathsf T=N\mathsf D^{-1}$, the map $\mathsf DN^{-1}C$ is a left inverse of $\mathsf T$. Applying it to the identity gives $\mathsf DN^{-1}CP_tF_t\mathsf S=P_sF_s$. The normalizations multiply to $2^{-(2\alpha^2-2)}2^{-1}2^{-1}=2^{-2\alpha^2}$, so $B_0P_tF_tA=2^{-2\alpha^2}P_sF_s$.

Harvey and van der Hoeven's algorithms give approximations $\widetilde{\mathsf S}'$, $\widetilde{\mathsf J}'$, $\widetilde{\mathsf D}'$ with errors $16p$, $3p^2/4$, $4$ and times $O(tp^{3/2+\delta}\alpha)$, $O(tp^{3/2+\delta}\alpha)$, $O(tp^{1+\delta})$
The selection $C$ picks an ordered subsequence (since $t/s>1$), and the indices are generated in order with $O(p)$ work each. So $C$ takes $O(tp)$ time with zero error
Contraction of the exact maps yields errors less than $16p<p^2$ and $4+3p^2/4<p^2$ (as $p>100$), and the costs add to $O(tp^{3/2+\delta}\alpha)$.

Start from $\widetilde v^{(0)}$, the rounding of $u/2$, and set $\widetilde v^{(i)}=\widetilde E\widetilde v^{(i-1)}$, so by induction every iterate stays in $\mathbb D_p^s$. The Neumann series is then evaluated as $\widetilde{\mathsf J}'u=\sum_{i=0}^{K-1}(-1)^i\widetilde v^{(i)}$, with every iterate kept in $\mathbb D_p$.

symbols.name: source length
symbols.meaning: The number of entries of the sequence whose transform is re-expressed.
symbols.quote: Gaussian resampling expresses the Fourier transform of a source length $s$ through the transform of a nearby larger power-of-two length $t$, so that only power-of-two transforms need a fast algorithm.

symbols.name: length gap
symbols.meaning: The relative gap t/s-1 between the padded and source lengths.

symbols.name: source permutation
symbols.meaning: The coordinate permutation (P_s u)_j = u_{tj} of length-s vectors.
symbols.quote: Define the permutations $(P_su)_j=u_{tj}$ and $(P_tv)_k=v_{-sk}$, with indices taken modulo $s$ and $t$.

symbols.name: target permutation
symbols.meaning: The coordinate permutation (P_t v)_k = v_{-sk} of length-t vectors.
symbols.quote: Define the permutations $(P_su)_j=u_{tj}$ and $(P_tv)_k=v_{-sk}$, with indices taken modulo $s$ and $t$.

symbols.name: input contraction
symbols.meaning: The linear contraction from length-s to length-t vectors in the resampling identity.
symbols.quote: The result is that there are linear contractions $A$, $B_0$ with $P_sF_s=2^{2\alpha^2}B_0P_tF_tA$.

symbols.name: output contraction
symbols.meaning: The linear contraction from length-t to length-s vectors in the resampling identity.
symbols.quote: The result is that there are linear contractions $A$, $B_0$ with $P_sF_s=2^{2\alpha^2}B_0P_tF_tA$.

symbols.name: source resampling map
symbols.meaning: Harvey and van der Hoeven's Gaussian map from length-s to length-t vectors with wide smear.
symbols.quote: Harvey and van der Hoeven's resampling maps (see [Established O(n log n) multiplier](hvdh-multiplier.md)) send length-$s$ vectors to length-$t$ vectors.

symbols.name: target resampling map
symbols.meaning: Harvey and van der Hoeven's Gaussian map from length-s to length-t vectors with narrow smear.
symbols.quote: Harvey and van der Hoeven's resampling maps (see [Established O(n log n) multiplier](hvdh-multiplier.md)) send length-$s$ vectors to length-$t$ vectors.

symbols.name: nearest index
symbols.quote: For each $j$ let $q_j$ be the integer nearest $tj/s$, and $\beta_j=tj/s-q_j$.

symbols.name: rounding offset
symbols.meaning: The offset tj/s - q_j from the nearest integer.
symbols.quote: For each $j$ let $q_j$ be the integer nearest $tj/s$, and $\beta_j=tj/s-q_j$.

symbols.name: coordinate selection
symbols.meaning: The map from length-t to length-s vectors that selects coordinates q_j.
symbols.quote: Let $C$ select coordinates from length-$t$ to length-$s$ vectors, $(Cv)_j=v_{q_j}$, and $(\mathsf Du)_j=e^{\pi\alpha^2\beta_j^2}u_j$.

symbols.name: Gaussian rescaling
symbols.meaning: The diagonal map multiplying u_j by e^{pi alpha^2 beta_j^2}.
symbols.quote: Let $C$ select coordinates from length-$t$ to length-$s$ vectors, $(Cv)_j=v_{q_j}$, and $(\mathsf Du)_j=e^{\pi\alpha^2\beta_j^2}u_j$.

symbols.name: near-identity map
symbols.meaning: The map C T D, whose diagonal entries are exactly 1.

symbols.name: off-diagonal part
symbols.quote: Let $E=N-I$ and $K=\lceil p/(\alpha^2\theta)\rceil$, the number of series terms kept.

symbols.name: series terms
symbols.meaning: The number of Neumann series terms kept.
symbols.quote: Let $E=N-I$ and $K=\lceil p/(\alpha^2\theta)\rceil$, the number of series terms kept.

symbols.name: p-bit grid
symbols.meaning: The grid of fixed-point Gaussian dyadic records with p fractional bits.
symbols.quote: Let $\mathbb D_p$ be the grid of [Fixed-point Gaussian dyadic records](fixed-point.md).
